title: Complete Data Engineering Roadmap
summary: A structured path from programming and SQL foundations through pipelines, Spark, Kafka, Airflow, and cloud data platforms to portfolio-ready projects.

overview.whatTheyDo: Data engineers design, build, and maintain reliable systems that move, transform, and store data so analysts, scientists, and products can use it with confidence.
overview.problemsSolved: They solve broken pipelines, inconsistent schemas, slow warehouse queries, late-arriving events, and the gap between raw source systems and trustworthy analytics tables.
overview.typicalDay: A typical day includes reviewing failed DAG runs, improving SQL or Spark jobs, modeling warehouse tables, coordinating with analysts on data contracts, and hardening monitoring and backfills.
overview.employers: Tech companies, fintech, e-commerce, healthcare, media, consulting firms, and any organization running a modern data stack or lakehouse.

prerequisites.title: Basic programming comfort
prerequisites.description: Ability to write simple scripts, use variables, loops, and functions. Prior Python experience helps but is not required.

prerequisites.title: Computer literacy
prerequisites.description: Comfort with files, folders, installing software, and using a terminal or command prompt.

prerequisites.title: Optional: intro CS concepts
prerequisites.description: Familiarity with algorithms, data structures, and how networks/APIs work will accelerate later stages.

stages.title: Programming Fundamentals
stages.description: Build the coding foundation every data engineer needs: Python, scripting, and version control with Git and GitHub.
stages.why_it_matters: Pipelines, transformations, and tooling are software. Strong fundamentals make every later stage faster and safer.

topics.title: Python for data work
topics.description: Learn Python syntax, data structures, file I/O, virtual environments, and writing readable modules for data scripts.
topics.why_it_matters: Python is the default language for ETL scripts, Airflow DAGs, Spark jobs, and cloud SDKs in data engineering.
project_ideas: Write a CSV cleaner that validates columns and writes Parquet-like output as CSV/JSON
Build a CLI that downloads a public API payload and saves normalized records

resources.title: Python 3 Official Tutorial
resources.description: Official language tutorial covering core syntax and standard library basics.

resources.title: Python for Everybody (freeCodeCamp)
resources.description: Beginner-friendly full course covering Python foundations.

resources.title: freeCodeCamp Python YouTube Course
resources.description: Long-form Python course suitable for absolute beginners.

topics.title: Git and GitHub
topics.description: Version control workflows: commits, branches, pull requests, and collaborating on pipeline code.
topics.why_it_matters: Production data code lives in Git. Reviews, rollbacks, and CI all depend on solid version control habits.
project_ideas: Put your Python scripts in a GitHub repo with a clear README and .gitignore
Practice a feature-branch PR workflow on a small data utility

resources.title: Git Documentation
resources.description: Official Git reference and everyday commands.

resources.title: GitHub Skills: Introduction to GitHub
resources.description: Hands-on GitHub learning path for issues, PRs, and collaboration.

resources.title: Pro Git Book
resources.description: Free official Pro Git book for deeper understanding.

topics.title: Scripting and Linux basics
topics.description: Navigate the shell, pipe commands, schedule simple jobs, and manage files used by data workflows.
topics.why_it_matters: Most data platforms are Linux-based. Shell fluency speeds debugging, deployments, and local pipeline work.
project_ideas: Write a bash script that downloads files, validates sizes, and logs results
Create a Makefile or simple shell entrypoints for your Python ETL

resources.title: GNU Bash Manual
resources.description: Official Bash reference for scripting and interactive use.

resources.title: The Linux Command Line (free book)
resources.description: Practical introduction to Linux command-line tools.

stages.title: SQL and Databases
stages.description: Master SQL querying, joins, aggregations, window functions, and relational design with PostgreSQL.
stages.why_it_matters: SQL is the lingua franca of warehouses, lakehouses, and analytical transformations. Weak SQL blocks every later tool.

topics.title: SQL fundamentals and joins
topics.description: SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, JOIN types, subqueries, and writing correct multi-table queries.
topics.why_it_matters: Almost every warehouse transformation and data check is expressed in SQL first.
project_ideas: Solve a set of join/aggregation exercises against a sample retail schema
Reproduce business metrics with documented grain and filters

topics.description: RANK, ROW_NUMBER, LAG/LEAD, running totals, and readable CTE-based query design.
topics.why_it_matters: Window functions power ranking, sessionization, SCD helpers, and many warehouse marts.
project_ideas: Build cohort retention queries with window functions
Rewrite nested subqueries into CTEs and compare readability

resources.description: Official docs for window function syntax and framing.

topics.title: Relational design with PostgreSQL
topics.description: Normalization basics, keys, constraints, indexes, and designing schemas for analytics and ops.
topics.why_it_matters: Bad schemas create pipeline complexity forever. Good keys and constraints protect data quality.
project_ideas: Design a PostgreSQL schema for an e-commerce domain with FKs and indexes
Load sample CSVs and enforce uniqueness/check constraints

resources.title: PostgreSQL Documentation
resources.description: Complete PostgreSQL reference for DDL, DML, and administration.

resources.title: PostgreSQL Exercises

stages.title: Data Engineering Foundations
stages.description: Learn data formats, ETL vs ELT, dimensional modeling, warehouses, lakes, and data quality practices.
stages.why_it_matters: These concepts are the mental model behind every pipeline and platform you will build.

topics.title: Data formats and storage
topics.description: CSV, JSON, Avro, Parquet, compression, partitioning, and when columnar formats win.
topics.why_it_matters: Format and partition choices dominate cost and performance in lakes and Spark jobs.
project_ideas: Convert a large CSV dataset to Parquet with sensible partitions
Benchmark query times on row vs columnar layouts for the same dataset

resources.title: Apache Parquet Documentation
resources.description: Official Parquet format documentation.

resources.title: Apache Avro Specification
resources.description: Schema-based binary serialization used heavily in streaming systems.

topics.title: ETL, ELT, and data modeling
topics.description: Batch load patterns, star schemas, facts/dimensions, SCD basics, and layered raw/staging/marts design.
topics.why_it_matters: Modeling decisions determine whether analysts trust tables and whether pipelines stay maintainable.
project_ideas: Design a star schema for orders, customers, and products
Implement an idempotent load from raw files into staging and mart tables

resources.title: dbt Learn – Fundamentals
resources.description: Modern ELT transformation concepts with dbt Core.

resources.title: Kimball Group – Dimensional Modeling Techniques
resources.description: Classic dimensional modeling guidance used in warehouses.

topics.title: Warehouses, lakes, and data quality
topics.description: When to use warehouses vs lakes, quality checks, contracts, and documenting table ownership.
topics.why_it_matters: Untrusted data is unused data. Quality and ownership practices separate hobby pipelines from production platforms.
project_ideas: Add row-count, null-rate, and uniqueness checks to a warehouse load
Write a short data contract for a core fact table

resources.title: Great Expectations Documentation
resources.description: Open-source data quality and validation framework.

resources.title: AWS Data Lakes and Analytics Overview
resources.description: Cloud vendor overview of lake and analytics building blocks.

stages.title: Data Processing
stages.description: Process large datasets with Apache Spark and learn streaming foundations with Apache Kafka.
stages.why_it_matters: When data outgrows a single database, distributed batch and streaming systems become required skills.

topics.title: Apache Spark and batch processing
topics.description: DataFrames, transformations/actions, partitions, shuffles, joins, and reading Parquet at scale.
topics.why_it_matters: Spark remains a core engine for large-scale batch ETL and lakehouse processing.
project_ideas: Rewrite a pandas ETL as a PySpark job over multi-GB files
Use the Spark UI to explain and reduce shuffle-heavy stages

resources.title: Apache Spark Documentation
resources.description: Official Spark docs including SQL and DataFrame APIs.

resources.title: PySpark Overview
resources.description: Python API guide for Spark applications.

resources.title: Spark Tutorial (freeCodeCamp)

topics.title: Distributed computing concepts
topics.description: Parallelism, fault tolerance, partitioning strategies, skew, and cost/performance trade-offs.
topics.why_it_matters: Without these concepts, Spark jobs are slow, expensive, and mysterious when they fail.
project_ideas: Experiment with repartition vs coalesce on a skewed dataset
Document shuffle sources in a join-heavy pipeline

resources.title: Spark Programming Guide
resources.description: Core Spark programming model and execution concepts.

topics.title: Streaming fundamentals with Kafka
topics.description: Topics, partitions, producers/consumers, consumer groups, and event-driven pipeline patterns.
topics.why_it_matters: Real-time and near-real-time products depend on durable event logs and streaming consumers.
project_ideas: Produce synthetic click events to Kafka and consume them into a table
Demonstrate consumer group rebalancing with multiple consumers

resources.description: Official Kafka intro, APIs, and operations guides.

resources.title: Kafka Introduction

resources.title: Confluent Kafka Tutorials
resources.description: Hands-on Kafka tutorials from Confluent.

stages.title: Workflow Orchestration
stages.description: Schedule and monitor pipelines with Apache Airflow: DAGs, retries, sensors, and operational hygiene.
stages.why_it_matters: Unscheduled scripts do not make a platform. Orchestration turns jobs into reliable production workflows.

topics.title: Apache Airflow fundamentals
topics.description: DAGs, operators, task dependencies, scheduling intervals, and local Airflow development.
topics.why_it_matters: Airflow is widely used to coordinate warehouse loads, Spark submits, and multi-step data workflows.
project_ideas: Create a daily Airflow DAG that extracts, loads, and validates a public dataset
Add sensors and email/Slack failure notifications to a DAG

resources.title: Apache Airflow Documentation
resources.description: Official Airflow docs for DAGs, operators, and deployment.

resources.title: Airflow Tutorial
resources.description: Getting started tutorial for writing your first DAGs.

topics.title: Scheduling, monitoring, and error handling
topics.description: Retries, backfills, SLAs, idempotency, catching failed tasks, and making pipelines re-runnable.
topics.why_it_matters: Production data work is mostly operations: recovering safely from failures without duplicating facts.
project_ideas: Make a load idempotent using MERGE/UPSERT semantics and DAG retries
Implement a backfill DAG for historical date partitions

resources.title: Airflow Best Practices
resources.description: Official guidance for DAG design and operational patterns.

resources.title: Astronomer Learn – Airflow
resources.description: Practical Airflow lessons and patterns.

stages.title: Cloud Infrastructure
stages.description: Learn cloud storage, compute, managed data services, IAM, and security patterns on a major cloud (AWS-focused with transferable concepts).
stages.why_it_matters: Most modern data platforms run on cloud object storage and managed warehouses or compute engines.

topics.title: Cloud storage and data services
topics.description: Object storage (S3), warehouses/query engines, and managed ingestion/transform services.
topics.why_it_matters: Landing zones, lake layers, and warehouse loads nearly always start with cloud object storage.
project_ideas: Land raw files in S3 with a date partition layout and query them with Athena or Spark

resources.title: Amazon Athena User Guide

resources.title: AWS Glue Developer Guide
resources.description: Managed ETL and catalog services on AWS.

topics.title: Permissions, security, and cost awareness
topics.description: IAM least privilege, encryption basics, secrets handling, and watching data-platform spend.
topics.why_it_matters: Over-privileged roles and unbounded scans are common production failures in data teams.
project_ideas: Create an IAM policy that only allows read access to one raw prefix
Estimate query cost before and after partition pruning

resources.title: AWS IAM User Guide
resources.description: Identity and access management fundamentals on AWS.

resources.title: Google Cloud Storage Documentation
resources.description: Comparable object storage concepts on GCP.

stages.title: Advanced Concepts
stages.description: Lakehouse architecture, governance, performance tuning, scalable pipeline design, and observability.
stages.why_it_matters: Senior data engineers own platform reliability, cost, and trust—not only individual jobs.

topics.title: Lakehouse and table formats
topics.description: Delta Lake / Iceberg concepts, ACID on object storage, time travel, and schema evolution.
topics.why_it_matters: Open table formats unify batch/streaming and warehouse-like reliability on lakes.
project_ideas: Build a medallion (bronze/silver/gold) pipeline with a table format
Demonstrate time travel and schema evolution on a sample table

resources.description: Official Delta Lake docs for lakehouse table semantics.

resources.title: Apache Iceberg Documentation
resources.description: Open table format docs for large analytic tables.

topics.title: Governance, optimization, and observability
topics.description: Lineage, access controls, query/job tuning, metrics, logs, and alerting for pipelines.
topics.why_it_matters: Without governance and observability, scale turns into silent data incidents.
project_ideas: Add structured logging and success/failure metrics to a pipeline
Create a runbook for a failed daily load including rollback steps

resources.title: OpenLineage Documentation
resources.description: Open standard for data lineage collection.

resources.title: Datadog Data Observability Concepts
resources.description: Vendor-neutral ideas for monitoring data pipelines and freshness.

stages.title: Real-World Projects
stages.description: Ship beginner through advanced portfolio projects that prove end-to-end data engineering skills.
stages.why_it_matters: Employers hire evidence. Projects that run, recover, and are explained well beat tool checklists.

topics.title: Beginner and intermediate projects
topics.description: Build smaller pipelines that still demonstrate modeling, tests, and documentation.
topics.why_it_matters: Early projects cement SQL/Python habits and give you artifacts for interviews quickly.

topics.description: Combine batch/streaming, cloud storage, orchestration, and BI-facing marts for a business scenario.
topics.why_it_matters: Capstone projects show you can own a domain problem, not just a single technology.
project_ideas: E-commerce clickstream: Kafka → Spark/Flink → lakehouse → dashboard metrics
Finance-style SCD Type 2 dimensions with incremental loads and reconciliation reports

stages.description: Prepare portfolio, GitHub presence, interview skills (SQL, coding, system design), and applications.
stages.why_it_matters: Skills alone are not enough—clear evidence and interview readiness turn learning into offers.

topics.why_it_matters: Recruiters and hiring managers often see your repos before they see you.

Record a short walkthrough video of a DAG and warehouse mart

topics.why_it_matters: Data engineering interviews stress correctness under constraints and clear architectural reasoning.
project_ideas: Timed SQL drills with window functions and tricky joins
Whiteboard a batch + streaming order analytics platform and defend trade-offs

title: Complete Backend Engineering Roadmap
summary: Learn to design and ship reliable APIs, databases, auth, messaging, and production services that power applications at scale.

overview.whatTheyDo: Backend engineers build server-side systems: APIs, business logic, data storage, authentication, background jobs, and integrations that clients and other services depend on.
overview.problemsSolved: They solve slow endpoints, inconsistent data, auth gaps, brittle integrations, and reliability issues that appear when traffic and complexity grow.
overview.typicalDay: Designing API contracts, writing service code and tests, tuning SQL, reviewing PRs, investigating production incidents, and collaborating with frontend and platform teams.
overview.employers: Product companies, startups, banks, SaaS platforms, marketplaces, and any org building multi-user applications.
fundamentalSkills: A backend language (Node, Go, Java, Python, etc.)

prerequisites.title: Programming basics
prerequisites.description: Comfort with variables, functions, data structures, and debugging in at least one language.

prerequisites.title: How the web works
prerequisites.description: High-level understanding of browsers, HTTP requests, and client/server roles.

stages.title: Language and tooling foundations
stages.description: Pick a primary backend language and master its tooling, modules, testing, and package ecosystem.
stages.why_it_matters: Backend quality starts with language fluency and disciplined project structure.

topics.title: Core language skills
topics.description: Types/collections, error handling, concurrency basics, and idiomatic project layout.
topics.why_it_matters: Service code must be readable, testable, and safe under failure.
project_ideas: Build a CLI task manager with persistence and tests
Implement retry/backoff utilities with unit tests

resources.title: Node.js Documentation
resources.description: Official Node.js API and guides.

resources.title: Go Tour
resources.description: Interactive introduction to the Go language.

resources.title: Python Docs – Tutorial
resources.description: Official Python tutorial for backend scripting and services.

topics.title: Git, testing, and package management
topics.description: Version control, unit/integration tests, dependency management, and linting.
topics.why_it_matters: Production teams ship through reviews, CI, and automated tests.
project_ideas: Add CI that runs lint + tests on every PR
Write table-driven tests for core domain logic

resources.title: Jest Documentation
resources.description: Popular JavaScript testing framework docs.

stages.title: HTTP, APIs, and web protocols
stages.description: Understand HTTP semantics, REST design, status codes, validation, and API documentation.
stages.why_it_matters: APIs are the product surface for most backend systems.

topics.title: HTTP and REST
topics.description: Methods, headers, status codes, idempotency, pagination, and resource modeling.
topics.why_it_matters: Correct HTTP design reduces client bugs and integration pain.
project_ideas: Design a versioned REST API for a bookstore
Add OpenAPI docs and request validation

topics.title: GraphQL and alternative API styles
topics.description: When GraphQL, RPC, or event-driven APIs fit better than pure REST.
topics.why_it_matters: Backend engineers choose contracts based on client needs and coupling costs.
project_ideas: Expose a small GraphQL schema over an existing REST domain
Compare N+1 risks and fix them with batching

stages.title: Databases and data modeling
stages.description: Model relational data, write efficient SQL, and understand transactions and indexing.
stages.why_it_matters: Most backend correctness and performance problems live in the database layer.

topics.title: SQL and PostgreSQL
topics.description: Schema design, joins, indexes, transactions, and migrations.
topics.why_it_matters: Relational databases remain the default system of record.
project_ideas: Model users, roles, and orders with migrations and seed data
Explain query plans for a slow endpoint and add an index

topics.title: ORMs, migrations, and consistency
topics.description: Use ORMs carefully, manage schema changes, and reason about isolation levels.
topics.why_it_matters: Schema drift and race conditions create subtle production bugs.
project_ideas: Implement optimistic locking for concurrent updates
Add a reversible migration strategy for a live table change

stages.title: Authentication, authorization, and security
stages.description: Secure sessions/tokens, password handling, OAuth, RBAC, and common web vulnerabilities.
stages.why_it_matters: A broken auth layer can invalidate an otherwise excellent service.

topics.title: AuthN and AuthZ patterns
topics.description: Sessions, JWT trade-offs, OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect, API keys, and RBAC.
topics.why_it_matters: Almost every product API needs trustworthy identity and permission checks.
project_ideas: Implement email/password auth with hashed passwords and refresh rotation
Add role-based guards to protected routes

topics.title: Application security basics
topics.description: Injection, XSS via APIs, CSRF, secrets management, and dependency hygiene.
topics.why_it_matters: Security is a backend responsibility, not a later add-on.
project_ideas: Threat-model a public API and document mitigations
Scan dependencies and fix high-severity advisories

stages.title: Caching, queues, and async work
stages.description: Use Redis, message queues, and background workers for speed and reliability.
stages.why_it_matters: Not everything belongs in a request/response path.

topics.title: Caching with Redis
topics.description: Cache-aside patterns, TTLs, invalidation, and avoiding stampeding herds.
topics.why_it_matters: Caching is the fastest way to cut latency and database load when applied carefully.
project_ideas: Cache hot read endpoints with explicit invalidation
Measure p95 latency before and after caching

topics.title: Background jobs and messaging
topics.description: Queues, retries, dead-letter handling, and at-least-once processing pitfalls.
topics.why_it_matters: Emails, webhooks, exports, and fan-out work need durable async execution.
project_ideas: Build an email/notification worker with retries and idempotency keys
Process webhook events asynchronously with a DLQ

stages.title: Architecture, scalability, and observability
stages.description: Design services that scale, fail gracefully, and can be debugged in production.
stages.why_it_matters: Senior backend work is about operability as much as features.

topics.title: Service design and scaling patterns
topics.description: Stateless services, rate limiting, circuit breakers, horizontal scaling, and data partitioning basics.
topics.why_it_matters: Growth exposes design shortcuts that were invisible at low traffic.
project_ideas: Add rate limiting and structured error budgets to an API
Design a read-heavy feed service with caching and pagination

topics.title: Logging, metrics, and tracing
topics.description: Structured logs, RED/USE metrics, distributed tracing, and on-call readiness.
topics.why_it_matters: You cannot fix what you cannot see.
project_ideas: Instrument an API with request IDs, latency metrics, and error rates
Add OpenTelemetry tracing across two services

stages.title: Projects and career preparation
stages.description: Ship portfolio services and prepare for backend interviews and system design.
stages.why_it_matters: Demonstrable systems and clear explanations convert skills into offers.

topics.title: Portfolio backend projects
topics.description: End-to-end APIs with auth, persistence, tests, Docker, and docs.
topics.why_it_matters: Hiring managers look for production judgment, not toy CRUD alone.
project_ideas: URL shortener with analytics, rate limits, and Redis cache
Multi-tenant notes API with RBAC, webhooks, and worker jobs

topics.title: Interview and system design prep
topics.description: Practice coding, SQL, and designing APIs/storage under constraints.
topics.why_it_matters: Backend interviews emphasize trade-offs, failure modes, and clear communication.
project_ideas: Write design docs for a rate limiter and a notification system
Timed SQL + coding practice set twice a week

title: Complete Frontend Engineering Roadmap
summary: Master HTML, CSS, JavaScript, modern frameworks, accessibility, performance, and product UI craft from first principles to production apps.

overview.whatTheyDo: Frontend engineers build the interfaces people use—components, pages, client-side state, and the glue between design systems and APIs.
overview.problemsSolved: They solve confusing UX, slow pages, inaccessible UIs, brittle components, and inconsistent experiences across devices.
overview.typicalDay: Implementing UI from designs, refining component APIs, fixing performance/a11y issues, writing tests, and collaborating with design and backend.
overview.employers: SaaS companies, consumer apps, agencies, e-commerce, media, and design-system-heavy product orgs.

prerequisites.title: Basic computer skills
prerequisites.description: Comfort installing tools, using a browser DevTools panel, and editing text files.

prerequisites.title: Willingness to learn visual craft
prerequisites.description: Frontend work sits at the intersection of engineering and UX quality.

stages.title: Web foundations
stages.description: Learn semantic HTML, modern CSS, and how browsers render pages.
stages.why_it_matters: Frameworks sit on top of the web platform—foundations transfer forever.

topics.title: Semantic HTML
topics.description: Document structure, forms, landmarks, and accessible markup defaults.
topics.why_it_matters: Good HTML is the cheapest accessibility and SEO win.
project_ideas: Build a multi-page marketing site with semantic landmarks
Recreate a complex form with native validation

topics.title: Modern CSS layout and styling
topics.description: Flexbox, Grid, responsive design, custom properties, and cascade layers basics.
topics.why_it_matters: Most UI polish and responsive bugs are CSS problems.
project_ideas: Build a responsive dashboard layout with CSS Grid
Create a themeable component using CSS variables

resources.title: CSS Tricks – A Complete Guide to Flexbox

stages.title: JavaScript and TypeScript
stages.description: Language fundamentals, DOM APIs, async patterns, and typing for safer UI code.
stages.why_it_matters: Frontend application logic and framework code are JavaScript/TypeScript.

topics.title: JavaScript language and DOM
topics.description: ES modules, promises/async, events, fetch, and DOM manipulation.
topics.why_it_matters: You need to debug the runtime beneath React or Vue.
project_ideas: Vanilla JS todo app with localStorage
Infinite scroll list using Intersection Observer

topics.title: TypeScript for UI code
topics.description: Types, generics, narrowing, and typing component props/events.
topics.why_it_matters: TypeScript catches entire classes of UI contract bugs early.
project_ideas: Migrate a JS app to TypeScript
Type a design-system Button/Input API strictly

stages.title: Modern UI frameworks
stages.description: Build component-driven apps with React (or equivalent) and routing/state patterns.
stages.why_it_matters: Most product frontends are framework applications, not static pages.

topics.title: React fundamentals
topics.description: Components, props, state, effects, and composition patterns.
topics.why_it_matters: React remains a dominant production UI library.
project_ideas: Build a multi-route SPA with React Router
Create a reusable data table with sorting/filtering

topics.title: State, data fetching, and app structure
topics.description: Server/client state boundaries, caching, forms, and folder architecture.
topics.why_it_matters: Poor state boundaries create unmaintainable UI trees.
project_ideas: Build a dashboard that caches API data and handles loading/error states
Implement optimistic updates for a like/bookmark action

stages.title: Accessibility and design systems
stages.description: Ship inclusive interfaces and reusable component libraries aligned with design.
stages.why_it_matters: Accessibility is quality. Design systems multiply team velocity.

topics.title: Web accessibility
topics.description: Keyboard support, ARIA carefully, focus management, contrast, and screen readers.
topics.why_it_matters: Inaccessible products exclude users and create legal/product risk.
project_ideas: Audit a page with Lighthouse/axe and fix critical issues
Build an accessible modal and dropdown from scratch

topics.title: Components and design tokens
topics.description: Variants, composition, tokens, and documenting a component library.
topics.why_it_matters: Consistent components keep large frontends coherent.
project_ideas: Create a small design system with Button, Input, Dialog
Document components in Storybook with a11y checks

stages.title: Performance, testing, and tooling
stages.description: Measure Core Web Vitals, write meaningful tests, and use modern frontend tooling.
stages.why_it_matters: Fast, tested UIs survive real users and real teams.

topics.title: Web performance
topics.description: Bundle size, rendering cost, images, caching, and Core Web Vitals.
topics.why_it_matters: Performance is UX and conversion.
project_ideas: Reduce LCP/CLS on a content-heavy page
Code-split a route and compare bundle reports

topics.title: Testing UI
topics.description: Unit, component, and end-to-end testing with user-centric assertions.
topics.why_it_matters: UI regressions are expensive; good tests protect critical flows.
project_ideas: Add Testing Library coverage for forms and auth-gated UI
Write a Playwright smoke test for checkout or onboarding

stages.title: Production apps and career prep
stages.description: Ship full product UIs and prepare portfolio/interview materials focused on frontend craft.

Create a content reader with offline caching and keyboard navigation

title: Complete DevOps Engineering Roadmap
summary: Learn Linux, CI/CD, containers, infrastructure as code, cloud operations, and reliability practices that ship software safely.

overview.whatTheyDo: DevOps engineers connect development and operations—automating builds, deployments, infrastructure, observability, and feedback loops so teams can release frequently with confidence.
overview.problemsSolved: They reduce manual releases, environment drift, long recovery times, and the wall between writing code and running it in production.
overview.typicalDay: Improving pipelines, reviewing Terraform/K8s changes, debugging failed deploys, hardening security defaults, and partnering with developers on operability.
overview.employers: Software companies, cloud-native startups, enterprises modernizing delivery, and managed service providers.

prerequisites.title: Basic programming or scripting
prerequisites.description: Ability to write simple scripts and read application code.

prerequisites.title: Networking fundamentals
prerequisites.description: IP, DNS, HTTP, and firewalls at a conceptual level help a lot.

stages.title: Linux, networking, and scripting
stages.description: Operate systems from the shell and automate repetitive tasks.
stages.why_it_matters: Cloud VMs and containers still behave like Linux machines underneath.

topics.title: Linux administration essentials
topics.description: Processes, permissions, systemd, networking tools, and log inspection.
topics.why_it_matters: Incident response often starts with SSH and logs.
project_ideas: Provision a Linux VM and harden SSH + firewall basics
Write runbooks for common service failure symptoms

topics.title: Bash and Python automation
topics.description: Script deployments, health checks, and glue between tools.
topics.why_it_matters: Automation is the core DevOps habit.
project_ideas: Script blue/green smoke checks after deploy
Automate certificate expiry alerts

stages.title: Version control and CI/CD
stages.description: Build automated pipelines that test and deliver software continuously.
stages.why_it_matters: Reliable delivery pipelines are the daily product of DevOps work.

topics.title: Git workflows for teams
topics.description: Branching strategies, protected branches, code review, and release tags.
topics.why_it_matters: Delivery quality starts with how code enters the mainline.
project_ideas: Set up branch protection + required checks
Document a trunk-based or GitHub Flow release process

topics.title: Continuous integration and delivery
topics.description: Build, test, artifact, deploy stages; secrets; environments; progressive delivery.
topics.why_it_matters: Manual releases do not scale and are risky.
project_ideas: Create a CI pipeline that builds, tests, and publishes a container image
Add staging → production promotion with approvals

stages.title: Containers and orchestration
stages.description: Package apps with Docker and run them on Kubernetes.
stages.why_it_matters: Containers are the default deployment unit for modern services.

topics.title: Docker fundamentals
topics.description: Images, layers, multi-stage builds, registries, and local compose stacks.
topics.why_it_matters: Consistent runtime environments eliminate works-on-my-machine failures.
project_ideas: Containerize a web API with a multi-stage Dockerfile
Compose app + database + reverse proxy locally

topics.title: Kubernetes basics
topics.description: Pods, Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps/Secrets, and rolling updates.
topics.why_it_matters: Kubernetes is the common control plane for container workloads.
project_ideas: Deploy an app to a local cluster (kind/minikube) with health probes
Perform a rolling update and a rollback

stages.title: Infrastructure as code and cloud
stages.description: Provision reproducible infrastructure with Terraform and cloud services.
stages.why_it_matters: ClickOps drifts; IaC is reviewable, repeatable, and auditable.

topics.title: Terraform and IaC workflows
topics.description: Providers, state, modules, plans/applies, and remote backends.
topics.why_it_matters: IaC is how modern teams manage cloud estates.
project_ideas: Terraform a VPC, subnet, and compute instance
Split reusable modules for network and app tiers

topics.title: Cloud platform foundations
topics.description: IAM, networking, compute, storage, and managed Kubernetes on one major cloud.
topics.why_it_matters: DevOps work is inseparable from cloud primitives.
project_ideas: Deploy a container app to a managed Kubernetes service
Implement least-privilege IAM for a deploy role

stages.title: Observability, reliability, and security
stages.description: Monitor systems, respond to incidents, and bake in security defaults.
stages.why_it_matters: Shipping is incomplete without knowing production health.

topics.title: Metrics, logs, and alerts
topics.description: Prometheus/Grafana-style metrics, log aggregation, SLOs, and actionable alerts.
topics.why_it_matters: Noisy or silent alerting both cause outages to last longer.
project_ideas: Define SLIs/SLOs for an API and wire alerts
Build a Grafana dashboard for latency and error rate

topics.title: DevSecOps basics
topics.description: Secrets management, image scanning, policy as code, and supply-chain hygiene.
topics.why_it_matters: Security failures in the pipeline become production breaches.
project_ideas: Scan container images in CI and fail on critical CVEs
Move secrets out of env files into a secrets manager

stages.title: Projects and career preparation
stages.description: Build a delivery platform portfolio and prepare for DevOps interviews.
stages.why_it_matters: Employers hire demonstrated automation and operational judgment.

topics.title: End-to-end delivery projects
topics.description: From git push to monitored production with IaC and rollback paths.
topics.why_it_matters: Capstone platforms show you can own the delivery lifecycle.
project_ideas: Full stack app with GitHub Actions, Terraform, Docker, K8s, and Grafana
GitOps-style deploy using a pull-based controller

topics.title: Interview prep
topics.description: Linux troubleshooting, CI/CD design, Kubernetes scenarios, and incident stories.
topics.why_it_matters: DevOps interviews are scenario-heavy and practical.
project_ideas: Write postmortems for two simulated outages
Practice whiteboard: design a CI/CD system for microservices

title: Complete Machine Learning Engineering Roadmap
summary: Progress from Python and math foundations through classical ML, deep learning, MLOps, and production model serving.

overview.whatTheyDo: Machine learning engineers turn data and models into reliable production systems—feature pipelines, training jobs, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring.
overview.problemsSolved: They bridge the gap between notebooks and production: data leakage, brittle training, silent model drift, and unscalable inference.
overview.typicalDay: Improving datasets/features, running experiments, reviewing metrics, packaging models, debugging serving latency, and partnering with data scientists and platform teams.
overview.employers: Tech product companies, ads/recommendation orgs, fintech, healthcare AI teams, and ML platform groups.

prerequisites.title: Programming comfort
prerequisites.description: Python basics and willingness to write clean, tested code—not only notebooks.

prerequisites.title: Math readiness
prerequisites.description: High-school algebra plus willingness to learn probability, linear algebra, and calculus intuition.

stages.title: Python, data, and math foundations
stages.description: Build the scientific Python stack and the math intuition ML depends on.
stages.why_it_matters: Every later framework assumes NumPy/pandas fluency and statistical literacy.

topics.title: Scientific Python
topics.description: NumPy, pandas, matplotlib/seaborn, and reproducible environments.
topics.why_it_matters: Data wrangling quality dominates model quality.
project_ideas: Exploratory analysis report on a public tabular dataset
Build reusable data-cleaning utilities with tests

resources.description: Official NumPy reference and user guide.

resources.title: pandas Documentation
resources.description: DataFrame APIs and analysis workflows.

resources.title: Python Data Science Handbook

topics.title: Probability and linear algebra intuition
topics.description: Distributions, expectation, variance, vectors/matrices, and gradients at a practical level.
topics.why_it_matters: You cannot debug loss curves or embeddings without this vocabulary.
project_ideas: Simulate sampling distributions and confidence intervals
Implement linear regression with NumPy and compare to sklearn

resources.title: 3Blue1Brown – Essence of Linear Algebra

stages.description: Supervised/unsupervised algorithms, metrics, validation, and feature engineering.
stages.why_it_matters: Many production problems are still best solved with classical models.

topics.title: Supervised learning and evaluation
topics.description: Linear/logistic models, trees/ensembles, cross-validation, and metric selection.
topics.why_it_matters: Wrong metrics and leakage create models that look good and fail live.

resources.description: Compose transformers and estimators safely.

resources.title: Kaggle Intermediate ML Course

stages.description: Neural networks, modern frameworks, and common architectures for vision/text.
stages.why_it_matters: Deep learning powers representation learning for complex unstructured data.

topics.description: Tensors, autograd, training loops, regularization, and GPU basics.
topics.why_it_matters: PyTorch is a dominant framework for research-to-production ML engineering.

resources.description: Official beginner-to-advanced PyTorch tutorials.

stages.why_it_matters: Without experiment hygiene, teams cannot iterate or audit models.

title: Complete AI Engineering Roadmap
summary: Learn to build LLM-powered applications: prompting, retrieval, agents, evaluation, safety, and production AI systems.

overview.whatTheyDo: AI engineers design and ship applications that use foundation models—RAG systems, agents, tool-calling workflows, eval harnesses, and productized AI features.
overview.problemsSolved: They solve brittle prompts, hallucinations, weak retrieval, missing evaluations, high latency/cost, and unsafe model behavior in user-facing products.
overview.typicalDay: Iterating prompts and retrieval, wiring tools/APIs, measuring evals, optimizing cost/latency, and collaborating with product on AI UX.
overview.employers: Startups building AI products, enterprise AI platform teams, SaaS companies adding copilots, and applied research engineering groups.

prerequisites.title: Software engineering basics
prerequisites.description: Comfort building APIs/apps and using Git. AI engineering is applied software work.

prerequisites.title: Python fluency
prerequisites.description: Ability to write modules, call APIs, and handle async/data processing in Python.

stages.title: Software and LLM foundations
stages.description: Strengthen backend/Python skills and understand how modern LLMs are used via APIs.
stages.why_it_matters: AI features fail when the surrounding software is weak.

topics.title: Python services for AI apps
topics.description: APIs, async I/O, packaging, environment/secrets, and structured logging.
topics.why_it_matters: Most AI systems are services that call models and tools.
project_ideas: Build a FastAPI service that proxies chat completions with streaming
Add request tracing IDs and token-usage logging

topics.title: LLM API fundamentals
topics.description: Tokens, context windows, temperature, tool/function calling, and streaming responses.
topics.why_it_matters: Product behavior depends on understanding model interfaces and constraints.
project_ideas: Compare temperature/top-p effects on a fixed prompt suite
Implement tool calling for a calculator/search helper

stages.title: Prompting, structured outputs, and UX
stages.description: Design prompts and product interactions that are reliable for users.
stages.why_it_matters: Prompting is product logic for LLM apps.

topics.title: Prompt engineering patterns
topics.description: System prompts, few-shot examples, constraints, and decomposition strategies.
topics.why_it_matters: Clear instructions and examples reduce variance and hallucinations.
project_ideas: Create a prompt library with versioning for a support assistant
Build a grader that scores prompt variants on a fixed dataset

topics.title: Structured outputs and guardrails
topics.description: JSON schemas, validation, refusal handling, and safe tool execution boundaries.
topics.why_it_matters: Downstream systems need predictable machine-readable outputs.
project_ideas: Force structured extraction into a Zod/Pydantic schema with retries
Add policy checks before executing side-effecting tools

stages.title: Embeddings, retrieval, and RAG
stages.description: Ground model responses in your data with embeddings and retrieval pipelines.
stages.why_it_matters: RAG is the practical path to domain-specific AI without full fine-tuning.

topics.title: Embeddings and vector search
topics.description: Chunking, embedding models, similarity search, and vector database basics.
topics.why_it_matters: Retrieval quality usually dominates generation quality in RAG apps.
project_ideas: Index a documentation corpus and evaluate top-k retrieval
Experiment with chunk sizes and overlap on answer faithfulness

topics.title: RAG system design
topics.description: Ingestion, hybrid search, reranking, citations, and failure modes.
topics.why_it_matters: Naive RAG fails on real enterprise corpora without careful design.
project_ideas: Build a docs Q&A bot with source citations
Add hybrid keyword + vector retrieval and compare eval scores

stages.title: Agents, tools, and orchestration
stages.description: Compose multi-step AI workflows that call tools and external systems safely.
stages.why_it_matters: Many product features need planning, memory, and tool use—not a single prompt.

topics.title: Tool-using agents
topics.description: Function calling, planner/executor patterns, memory, and human-in-the-loop.
topics.why_it_matters: Agents amplify capability and risk; design must be deliberate.
project_ideas: Build an agent that can search docs, call an API, and draft an answer
Add confirmation steps before write actions

topics.title: Workflow orchestration frameworks
topics.description: When to use chains vs graphs vs plain code for maintainable AI systems.
topics.why_it_matters: Framework choices affect debuggability and production ownership.
project_ideas: Rebuild a LangChain flow in plain Python and compare clarity
Add tracing for each agent step and tool call

stages.title: Evaluation, safety, cost, and production
stages.description: Measure quality, control risk, and operate AI features under latency and budget constraints.
stages.why_it_matters: Without evals and ops, AI demos never become trustworthy products.

topics.title: Evaluation harnesses
topics.description: Golden sets, rubric/LLM-as-judge carefully, regression testing for prompts/RAG.
topics.why_it_matters: You cannot improve what you do not measure.
project_ideas: Create a 50-example eval set with automatic scoring
Block merges when eval scores regress beyond a threshold

topics.title: Safety, cost, and deployment
topics.description: Content filters, PII handling, caching, rate limits, model routing, and observability.
topics.why_it_matters: Production AI must be safe, affordable, and operable.
project_ideas: Add semantic cache + model routing by difficulty
Ship an AI feature with red-team prompts and refusal tests

stages.title: Portfolio and career preparation
stages.description: Ship AI products that demonstrate judgment beyond calling an API.
stages.why_it_matters: Employers want engineers who can evaluate and operate AI systems, not only demo them.

topics.title: AI product portfolio
topics.description: Full apps with RAG/agents, evals, tracing, and clear architecture write-ups.
topics.why_it_matters: Strong portfolios show product thinking and reliability.
project_ideas: Domain RAG assistant with citations, eval dashboard, and cost report
Internal copilot that uses tools against a real API with audit logs

topics.title: Interview readiness
topics.description: Explain RAG trade-offs, eval design, failure modes, and system diagrams.
topics.why_it_matters: AI engineer interviews emphasize practical system design and evaluation.
project_ideas: Whiteboard a customer-support AI architecture with safety controls
Prepare stories about debugging retrieval failures

title: Complete Cloud Engineering Roadmap
summary: Master cloud networking, IAM, compute, storage, IaC, containers, and operational excellence across major cloud platforms.

overview.whatTheyDo: Cloud engineers design, build, and operate cloud infrastructure—networking, identity, compute, storage, and platform services that applications run on.
overview.problemsSolved: They solve insecure defaults, sprawling accounts, unreliable deployments, cost overruns, and environments that cannot be reproduced.
overview.typicalDay: Writing Terraform, reviewing IAM policies, designing VPC architectures, automating provisioning, and supporting application teams with cloud landing zones.
overview.employers: Enterprises migrating to cloud, SaaS companies, consultancies, and cloud center-of-excellence teams.

prerequisites.title: Operating systems and networking basics
prerequisites.description: Comfort with Linux, IP addressing, DNS, and HTTP helps accelerate cloud learning.

prerequisites.title: Scripting ability
prerequisites.description: Bash or Python for automation and glue code.

stages.title: Cloud fundamentals and core services
stages.description: Learn shared responsibility, regions/AZs, and primary compute/storage/network building blocks.
stages.why_it_matters: Every architecture decision rests on these primitives.

topics.title: Cloud concepts and shared responsibility
topics.description: IaaS/PaaS/SaaS, regions, availability zones, and account/organization models.
topics.why_it_matters: Misunderstanding responsibility boundaries causes security and reliability gaps.
project_ideas: Map a sample app to IaaS vs PaaS choices and justify trade-offs
Create an account structure diagram for prod/non-prod

topics.title: Compute, storage, and databases
topics.description: VMs, managed containers, object storage, block storage, and managed databases.
topics.why_it_matters: Selecting the right service is half of cloud engineering.
project_ideas: Host a static site on object storage + CDN
Deploy an app VM with managed PostgreSQL

stages.title: Networking and identity
stages.description: Design VPCs/VNets, routing, load balancing, and least-privilege IAM.
stages.why_it_matters: Most cloud outages and breaches involve network or identity mistakes.

topics.title: Virtual networks, DNS, and load balancing
topics.description: Subnets, route tables, NAT, security groups/NSGs, DNS, and L4/L7 load balancers.
topics.why_it_matters: Applications cannot be reliable or secure without sound network design.
project_ideas: Build a public/private subnet architecture with a bastion pattern
Front an app with a load balancer and health checks

topics.title: IAM and access management
topics.description: Users/roles/policies, federation, service identities, and key management basics.
topics.why_it_matters: Identity is the primary security boundary in cloud.
project_ideas: Replace long-lived keys with role assumption
Write least-privilege policies for a deploy pipeline

stages.title: Infrastructure as code
stages.description: Provision and change cloud resources reproducibly with Terraform or cloud-native IaC.
stages.why_it_matters: Manual consoles do not scale and cannot be reviewed.

topics.title: Terraform for cloud provisioning
topics.description: State, modules, workspaces/backends, and policy checks.
topics.why_it_matters: IaC is the standard interface for cloud engineering teams.
project_ideas: Terraform a three-tier network + compute stack
Split environment configs for staging and production

topics.title: Cloud-native IaC options
topics.description: CloudFormation/Bicep/Pulumi overview and when each fits.
topics.why_it_matters: Enterprises often standardize on one IaC toolchain.
project_ideas: Recreate a small stack in a second IaC tool and compare DX
Add plan checks to CI for infrastructure PRs

stages.title: Containers, platform services, and automation
stages.description: Run workloads on containers/serverless and automate operational tasks.
stages.why_it_matters: Modern cloud engineering often means platforms for developers, not only VMs.

topics.title: Containers on cloud
topics.description: ECR/ACR/Artifact Registry, ECS/EKS/GKE/AKS basics, and serverless containers.
topics.why_it_matters: Application teams expect container platforms.
project_ideas: Deploy a containerized API to a managed container service
Add autoscaling and health checks

topics.description: Functions, queues, event buses, and managed workflow services.
topics.why_it_matters: Many cloud-native designs are event-driven and pay-per-use.
project_ideas: Build an image-processing pipeline with object storage events + functions
Implement async fan-out with a queue

stages.title: Reliability, cost, and security operations
stages.description: Operate cloud estates with monitoring, budgets, backups, and security baselines.
stages.why_it_matters: Cloud engineer success is measured in uptime, cost, and security posture.

title: Complete Cybersecurity Engineering Roadmap

overview.whatTheyDo: Cybersecurity engineers protect systems and data by designing controls, finding weaknesses, detecting threats, and helping organizations recover from incidents.
overview.problemsSolved: They reduce breach risk from misconfigurations, vulnerable software, weak identity controls, and slow detection/response.
overview.typicalDay: Reviewing architectures, hardening systems, analyzing alerts, validating remediations, writing detection rules, and advising engineering teams on secure design.
overview.employers: Enterprises, security consultancies, MSSPs, fintech, healthcare, government contractors, and product security teams.

prerequisites.title: IT or programming fundamentals

prerequisites.title: Ethical mindset
prerequisites.description: Security skills must be practiced legally on systems you own or have permission to test.

stages.title: Security foundations
stages.description: Learn core security principles, threat models, and cryptography basics.
stages.why_it_matters: Tools change; principles of confidentiality, integrity, and availability do not.

topics.title: Security principles and threat modeling
topics.description: CIA triad, least privilege, defense in depth, and STRIDE-style threat modeling.
topics.why_it_matters: Good engineers reason about risk before buying tools.

topics.why_it_matters: Crypto misuse is a frequent root cause of security failures.

Compare password hashing approaches and explain why unsalted hashes fail

resources.title: Cryptography I (Stanford Online / Coursera landing via Dan Boneh materials)

stages.title: Networking and operating systems for security
stages.description: Understand how packets, hosts, and identities actually work so you can defend them.
stages.why_it_matters: You cannot secure what you cannot explain.

topics.title: TCP/IP and network security controls
topics.description: Ports, protocols, firewalls, proxies, VPNs, and packet analysis basics.
topics.why_it_matters: Network paths define attack surface and detection opportunities.
project_ideas: Capture and analyze HTTP/DNS traffic in a lab
Configure host firewall rules for a least-privilege service profile

topics.title: Linux/Windows hardening essentials
topics.description: Permissions, services, logging, patching, and secure baseline configurations.
topics.why_it_matters: Endpoint and server hardening stops many commodity attacks.
project_ideas: Harden a Linux VM against a CIS-inspired checklist
Enable and review audit logs for privileged actions

stages.title: Application security
stages.description: Find and fix vulnerabilities in web and API applications.
stages.why_it_matters: Applications are a primary breach vector for modern organizations.

topics.title: OWASP Top Ten and secure coding
topics.description: Injection, broken auth, SSRF, access control flaws, and secure defaults.
topics.why_it_matters: Most exploited bugs are known classes with known mitigations.
project_ideas: Fix intentionally vulnerable lab apps (legally, locally)
Add security unit tests for authz checks

topics.title: Secure SDLC and dependency risk
topics.description: SAST/DAST concepts, SCA, secrets detection, and security in CI.
topics.why_it_matters: Security engineers scale by improving the development process.
project_ideas: Add dependency scanning and secret scanning to a sample repo
Write a secure code review guide for your stack

stages.title: Cloud and identity security
stages.description: Secure cloud estates and modern identity systems.
stages.why_it_matters: Identity and cloud misconfigurations dominate recent breach reports.

topics.title: Cloud security posture
topics.description: IAM least privilege, public exposure, encryption, logging, and benchmark alignments.
topics.why_it_matters: Cloud engineers and security engineers share this battleground.
project_ideas: Audit a lab cloud account for public buckets and admin roles
Enable cloud audit logs and alert on suspicious API calls

topics.title: Identity, SSO, and zero trust concepts
topics.description: MFA, federation, OAuth/OIDC risks, and device/user trust signals.
topics.why_it_matters: Stolen credentials remain one of the most effective attack methods.
project_ideas: Design an SSO + MFA architecture for a SaaS admin portal
Review OAuth redirect URI pitfalls in a sample app

stages.title: Detection, response, and blue team practice
stages.description: Detect attacks, investigate alerts, and respond with clear playbooks.
stages.why_it_matters: Prevention fails; detection and response limit damage.

topics.title: Logging, SIEM concepts, and detection engineering
topics.description: Telemetry sources, correlation, detections-as-code, and alert quality.
topics.why_it_matters: Security teams drown without high-signal detections.
project_ideas: Write detections for failed logins and impossible travel in a lab
Build a small log pipeline from apps to a searchable store

topics.title: Incident response basics
topics.description: Preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery, and lessons learned.
topics.why_it_matters: Incidents are when security engineering proves its value.
project_ideas: Write an IR playbook for ransomware-like symptoms in a lab
Run a tabletop exercise and capture action items

resources.title: NIST SP 800-61 Computer Security Incident Handling Guide

stages.title: Projects and career preparation
stages.description: Build a security portfolio ethically and prepare for security engineering interviews.
stages.why_it_matters: Demonstrated labs, write-ups, and judgment matter more than tool name-dropping.

topics.title: Home lab and portfolio write-ups
topics.description: Document legal labs, detections, hardening guides, and architecture reviews.
topics.why_it_matters: Hiring managers look for clear thinking and ethical practice.
project_ideas: Publish a hardened cloud lab architecture with detections
Write a case study remediating OWASP issues in a demo app

topics.title: Interview and certification paths
topics.description: Scenario interviews, plus optional certs (Security+, cloud security, OSCP-adjacent paths) chosen carefully.
topics.why_it_matters: Security interviews test reasoning under realistic constraints.
project_ideas: Practice explaining a breach postmortem using MITRE ATT&CK
Prepare a secure design review of a familiar system

title: Complete Full-Stack Engineering Roadmap
summary: Learn to ship complete products across UI, APIs, databases, auth, and deployment with a pragmatic full-stack workflow.

overview.whatTheyDo: Full-stack engineers own features end to end—user interface, server APIs, data models, and often deployment—so products move from idea to production quickly.
overview.problemsSolved: They reduce handoff friction between frontend and backend, close product gaps, and deliver coherent features without waiting on multiple teams.
overview.typicalDay: Implementing UI flows, writing API handlers, migrating schemas, wiring auth, fixing bugs across the stack, and deploying previews.
overview.employers: Startups, product squads in larger companies, agencies, and teams that value end-to-end ownership.

prerequisites.title: Basic programming
prerequisites.description: Comfort writing small programs and using the command line.

prerequisites.title: Curiosity about product UX
prerequisites.description: Full-stack work benefits from caring about both interface and data correctness.

stages.title: Web and JavaScript foundations
stages.description: Build confidence with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Git before frameworks.
stages.why_it_matters: Full-stack debugging constantly returns to web platform fundamentals.

topics.title: HTML, CSS, and responsive UI
topics.description: Semantic markup, Flexbox/Grid, and mobile-friendly layouts.
topics.why_it_matters: Users experience your backend through the UI first.
project_ideas: Build a responsive marketing page and dashboard shell
Recreate a settings form with accessible labels

topics.title: JavaScript and Git
topics.description: Language fundamentals, fetch/async, modules, and version control.
topics.why_it_matters: One language often spans both sides of a modern full-stack app.
project_ideas: Vanilla JS app that calls a public API
GitHub repo with meaningful commits and README

stages.title: Frontend application development
stages.description: Build interactive UIs with React/Next.js and solid state/data-fetching habits.
stages.why_it_matters: Most full-stack roles expect strong client application skills.

topics.title: React and component-driven UI
topics.description: Components, hooks, forms, routing, and composition.
topics.why_it_matters: Component models dominate product frontends.
project_ideas: Multi-page React app with authenticated routes stub
Reusable form components with validation

topics.title: Full-stack frameworks (Next.js)
topics.description: Routing, server/client components, and deploying app-router style projects.
topics.why_it_matters: Modern full-stack JS often lives in one framework codebase.
project_ideas: Build a Next.js CRUD app with server actions or route handlers
Add loading/error states and basic SEO metadata

stages.title: Backend APIs and databases
stages.description: Design APIs, model data in SQL, and keep server logic secure and tested.
stages.why_it_matters: Without solid data and API design, UIs become fragile.

topics.title: HTTP APIs and server logic
topics.description: REST handlers, validation, error shapes, and authorization checks.
topics.why_it_matters: The API is the contract between UI and data.
project_ideas: Build a notes API with ownership checks
Document endpoints with OpenAPI

topics.title: PostgreSQL and migrations
topics.description: Schema design, SQL queries, indexes, and migration tooling.
topics.why_it_matters: Full-stack features almost always involve durable data.
project_ideas: Model users/projects/tasks with foreign keys
Write migrations and seed scripts

stages.title: Auth, security, and product quality
stages.description: Add authentication, protect routes, and raise quality with tests and accessibility.
stages.why_it_matters: Shipping full features includes login, permissions, and trustworthiness.

topics.title: Authentication and sessions
topics.description: Email/password or OAuth, session cookies vs tokens, and route protection.
topics.why_it_matters: Most products are useless without identity.
project_ideas: Add Google OAuth and protected dashboard routes
Implement role-based UI and API guards

topics.title: Testing and accessibility
topics.description: Unit/integration/E2E tests and basic a11y checks across the stack.
topics.why_it_matters: Full-stack ownership means preventing regressions yourself.
project_ideas: Add Playwright coverage for signup → create → logout
Fix keyboard navigation issues in primary flows

stages.title: Deployment, DevOps lite, and observability
stages.description: Deploy apps, manage env vars, and watch production health at a practical level.
stages.why_it_matters: A feature is not done until it runs reliably for users.

topics.title: Deploying full-stack apps
topics.description: Hosting, databases-as-a-service, CI checks, and preview environments.
topics.why_it_matters: Full-stack engineers frequently own release plumbing on small teams.
project_ideas: Deploy an app with managed Postgres and environment secrets
Add CI for lint/test before deploy

topics.title: Basic monitoring and error tracking
topics.description: Logging, error reporting, and simple uptime checks.
topics.why_it_matters: You need visibility when production breaks after a full-stack change.
project_ideas: Add structured logs and an error tracker to your app
Create a simple status endpoint and uptime monitor

stages.title: Capstone projects and career prep
stages.description: Ship portfolio products that prove end-to-end ownership.
stages.why_it_matters: Full-stack hiring strongly favors complete shipped applications.

topics.title: End-to-end product projects
topics.description: Auth, CRUD, payments stub or teams features, polish, and deployment.
topics.why_it_matters: Portfolio apps should look and behave like real products.
project_ideas: SaaS-style project manager with members, roles, and activity feed
Content platform with blogging, bookmarks, and search

topics.title: Interview preparation
topics.description: JS/TS, React, SQL, system design for small apps, and take-home projects.
topics.why_it_matters: Interviews test breadth plus the ability to connect layers.
project_ideas: Practice explaining architecture of your best app in 10 minutes
Timed SQL + React bugfix drills

title: Complete Software Engineering Roadmap
summary: A role-agnostic path covering CS fundamentals, programming, software design, collaboration, systems thinking, and career readiness.

overview.whatTheyDo: Software engineers design, implement, test, and maintain software systems that solve user and business problems across many domains.
overview.problemsSolved: They turn ambiguous requirements into reliable programs, reduce complexity through design, and keep systems evolvable as needs change.
overview.typicalDay: Writing and reviewing code, clarifying requirements, debugging, testing, documenting trade-offs, and collaborating in an engineering team.
overview.employers: Technology companies of all sizes, banks, governments, startups, and any organization building software products or internal tools.

prerequisites.title: Motivation to build
prerequisites.description: Willingness to practice by writing real programs, not only watching tutorials.

prerequisites.title: Basic computer literacy
prerequisites.description: Installing tools, using files/folders, and learning from documentation.

stages.title: Programming fundamentals
stages.description: Learn one language deeply: syntax, problem decomposition, and debugging habits.
stages.why_it_matters: Everything else in software engineering builds on writing correct programs.

topics.title: Core programming skills
topics.description: Variables, control flow, functions, data structures, and modular code.
topics.why_it_matters: Clear fundamentals transfer across languages and stacks.
project_ideas: Build a CLI expense tracker with tests
Implement classic utilities (todo, parser, file organizer)

topics.title: Git and professional workflow
topics.description: Commits, branches, pull requests, code review etiquette, and issue tracking.
topics.why_it_matters: Software is a team sport; Git is the collaboration backbone.
project_ideas: Contribute a small fix to an open-source repo
Maintain a personal project with PR-based workflow

stages.title: Computer science essentials
stages.description: Data structures, algorithms, complexity, and how computers execute programs.
stages.why_it_matters: CS foundations improve design quality and interview readiness.

topics.title: Data structures and algorithms
topics.description: Arrays, hash maps, trees/graphs, sorting/searching, and Big-O reasoning.
topics.why_it_matters: Choosing the right structure prevents performance and correctness bugs.
project_ideas: Implement core data structures from scratch with tests
Solve curated algorithm problems with written explanations

topics.title: How computers and networks work
topics.description: Memory, processes, filesystems, OS basics, and HTTP/networking overview.
topics.why_it_matters: Debugging production systems requires systems intuition.
project_ideas: Trace a web request from browser to server logs
Write a short explainer of processes vs threads

stages.title: Building applications
stages.description: Apply fundamentals to web/backend/mobile-adjacent app building with databases.
stages.why_it_matters: Employers hire engineers who can ship working software.

topics.title: Application architecture basics
topics.description: Layering, APIs, MVC-like patterns, configuration, and dependency boundaries.
topics.why_it_matters: Structure keeps growing codebases maintainable.
project_ideas: Build a small web app with clear UI/API/data layers
Refactor a spaghetti script into modules with interfaces

resources.title: MariaDB / SQL learning via PostgreSQL docs

topics.title: Testing and quality
topics.description: Unit tests, integration tests, assertions, and debugging methodology.
topics.why_it_matters: Untested software becomes unchangeable software.
project_ideas: Achieve meaningful test coverage on a core module
Practice bisecting a regression with Git

stages.title: Software design and collaboration
stages.description: Write readable code, design for change, and work effectively on a team.
stages.why_it_matters: Senior impact comes from design and collaboration, not only coding speed.

topics.title: Clean code and design principles
topics.description: Naming, cohesion, SOLID-inspired principles, and pragmatic abstraction.
topics.why_it_matters: Readable design reduces bugs and onboarding time.
project_ideas: Refactor a project using clearer boundaries and names
Write ADRs for two non-trivial design decisions

topics.title: Team engineering practices
topics.description: Code review, documentation, agile rituals done usefully, and estimation basics.
topics.why_it_matters: Most software is built by teams with shared ownership.
project_ideas: Create a contribution guide for your project
Run a mock code review checklist on a friend's PR

stages.title: Systems, security, and production awareness
stages.description: Learn enough about systems, security, and operations to build responsible software.
stages.why_it_matters: Modern engineers cannot ignore how software runs and fails in production.

topics.title: Reliability and observability basics
topics.description: Logging, metrics, failure modes, retries, and graceful degradation.
topics.why_it_matters: Real users experience outages and latency, not only happy paths.
project_ideas: Add structured logging and health checks to an app
Document failure modes for a feature you built

topics.title: Security hygiene for engineers
topics.description: OWASP basics, secrets handling, dependency updates, and least privilege.
topics.why_it_matters: Every engineer shares security responsibility.
project_ideas: Audit a project for hardcoded secrets and fix them
Enable dependency scanning and resolve critical issues

stages.title: Specialization bridge and career preparation
stages.description: Choose a focus area (frontend, backend, mobile, data, etc.) and prepare for hiring.
stages.why_it_matters: Software engineer is broad; depth in a direction accelerates employment.

topics.title: Pick a specialization path
topics.description: Explore frontend, backend, mobile, data, or infrastructure and deepen deliberately.
topics.why_it_matters: General foundations plus one sharp edge is a strong career combo.
project_ideas: Ship two portfolio projects in your chosen specialization
Write a learning plan for the next 90 days with milestones

topics.title: Interviews, portfolio, and storytelling
topics.description: Coding interviews, behavioral stories, resume projects, and system design intro.
topics.why_it_matters: Getting hired requires communicating impact clearly.
project_ideas: Prepare STAR stories for teamwork, conflict, and debugging
Publish polished READMEs with architecture diagrams
